clue.text: Pub spirit to give Ironweed's Francis

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house, a pub
elan is dash, vigour or spirit

explanation.surface: A drink in the pub to hand to a man called Francis from a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Phelan is the down-and-out hero of William Kennedy's novel Ironweed.

clue.text: Dream lover has this girl's head spinning

parts.note: this girl's gives the possessive her

indicators.note: spinning turns the word for head round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to head for something is to aim at it

explanation.surface: A dreamt-of sweetheart sets a young woman's head in a whirl.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermia is one of the young lovers in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Hit book taken from Elia

indicators.note: taken from says the letter for book is removed from the essayist's real surname

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A best-seller lifted from the essays of Elia.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia is not a word to mine for letters but a pen name: Charles Lamb signed his Essays of Elia that way.
explanation.definitionFit: To lam someone is to thrash or strike them, an informal word for hit.

clue.text: Alan Paton's place of birth

definitions.meaning: the South African province where the author of Cry, the Beloved Country was born and lived
an adjective meaning relating to birth

explanation.surface: Where the South African novelist Alan Paton was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Paton was born in Pietermaritzburg in the old province of that name, and the adjective also means pertaining to birth.

clue.text: Lecturer Dixon's bold omitting the first vocal exercise

indicators.note: omitting the first says the opening letter of the word for bold is dropped

parts.note: plucky means brave or bold

indicators.note: vocal says the word for exercise is to be taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: gym is short for gymnastics, physical exercise

explanation.surface: A lecturer called Dixon is confident enough to skip the first warm-up for the voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocal exercise' reads as a singer's scale, but 'vocal' is the sound signal on 'exercise'. The 's of 'Dixon's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Dixon, the hapless young history lecturer, is the hero of Kingsley Amis's novel of that title.

clue.text: Literary Club member, Bennet, left a good century after Newton

indicators.note: after puts the good century following the unit symbol

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A member of a literary club departed well over a hundred years after the scientist Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton looks like Isaac, the scientist, but gives only N, the newton. 'after' places G and TON behind that N.
explanation.definitionFit: Bennet Langton was a founding member of Samuel Johnson's Literary Club, called simply the Club.

clue.text: Mirbeau's chambermaid and nieces let loose

indicators.note: let loose suggests the letters set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A French novelist's maid and some nieces are set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestine is the narrator of Octave Mirbeau's novel The Diary of a Chambermaid.

clue.text: A Macbeth victim is brought round in paediatric unit?

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the name for the children's ward

parts.note: a ward for the young is a children's hospital ward

indicators.note: brought round says the little word is is turned about so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone attacked in Macbeth is revived in a children's hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' looks like reviving a patient, fitting the hospital setting, but it is the reversal signal on 'is'; 'in' then places that inside the children's ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Young Siward, son of the English earl, is killed by Macbeth in single combat in the final act.

clue.text: In Carthage, Trojan spokesman's one uniform eaten by big cat, almost

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: eaten by puts the letter for uniform inside the shortened cat
almost says the last letter of the big cat is dropped

parts.note: a lioness is a female big cat
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Trojan envoy's dress is devoured by a lioness in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LIONESS to LIONES, and 'eaten by' puts U inside it to make LIONEUS. The 's in 'spokesman's' means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilioneus is the Trojan who speaks for Aeneas's shipwrecked men before Dido at Carthage in the Aeneid.

clue.text: The Outlaws creator's play, in court, being shown

indicators.note: in puts the word for play inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: to romp is to play boisterously
a show that is on is being shown or performed

explanation.surface: A writer's drama is being staged at a court.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'creator's' stands for 'is'. 'Play' looks like a drama to go with 'being shown', but here it means a romp.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmal Crompton wrote the Just William stories, in which William leads a gang called the Outlaws.

clue.text: A March groom's tale about a Babylonian city

indicators.note: about says the word for tale goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a tale can be a lie, as in telling tales
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A bridegroom in spring tells a story about an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: March looks like the month but names the family of sisters in Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Laurence, called Laurie, marries Amy March in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women and its sequel.

clue.text: Big beast excited lusty Phaedra's stepson

parts.note: a hippo is a hippopotamus, a big beast

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of lusty are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A large animal arouses passion in the stepson Phaedra lusted after.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Phaedra fell in love with Hippolytus, son of her husband Theseus by an earlier wife.

clue.text: On stage as character, maybe a king?

parts.note: an actor on stage as Hamlet is playing Hamlet
a card is an eccentric person, a character

explanation.surface: Acting a part, perhaps a royal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is one of the court cards in a pack, so it is an example of the thing defined.

clue.text: Weapon North Islander left behind

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A weapon belonging to someone from the north island, abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North Islander' looks like a New Zealander, but North gives N alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Gunn is the man marooned for years on the island in Stevenson's Treasure Island.

clue.text: Devious Titan originally appearing by chance

indicators.note: originally, read as in an original or novel way, tells us the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scheming giant first turns up quite by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like a first-letter signal on Titan, but the anagram uses all of DEVIOUS and TITAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adventitious happens or arrives accidentally rather than by design.

clue.text: Vishnu devotee has a viva arranged around noon

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround the letter for noon
arranged says the letters of has a viva are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A worshipper of Vishnu has an oral exam set for around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vaishnava tradition of Hinduism worships Vishnu as the supreme god, and a follower is so named.

clue.text: Book cut up in a part in Coriolanus

indicators.note: cut says the word for book loses its final letter

parts.note: a volume is a book

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the little word in is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A book has been cut to pieces for a role in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Volumnia is Coriolanus's formidable mother, a leading role in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: A lone pupil is misspelling a senator in Julius Caesar

indicators.note: misspelling suggests the letters of a lone pupil is are written out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A solitary schoolchild gets the name of a Roman senator wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Popilius Lena is the senator in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar whose words to Caesar alarm the conspirators.

clue.text: Perhaps Siwertz's opera but with all signs of energy removed

indicators.text: with all signs of energy removed
indicators.note: E is the physics symbol for energy, so every such letter is taken out of the opera's name

parts.note: Siegfried is the third opera of Wagner's Ring cycle

explanation.surface: Maybe an opera by a Swedish writer, but drained of all its energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Siwertz's own name as one example of the shorter form of the Wagner hero's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigfrid Siwertz was a Swedish novelist, and the first name is the form his name took.

clue.text: Baronet evicting a weird family of writers

indicators.note: weird says the remaining letters are put in a strange new order
evicting says the letter a is thrown out of the word baronet

explanation.surface: A titled landowner throws out a strange family of authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne made the Brontes the best-known literary family in English.

clue.text: An analyst's vessel holding Nitrogen

indicators.note: holding says the vessel contains the chemical symbol

parts.note: a jug is a vessel for liquid
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst's container has nitrogen in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Gustav Jung was the Swiss founder of analytical psychology, so a famous analyst.

clue.text: Abandoned like the ark on Ararat?

definitions.meaning: left stranded with no help, deserted
Noah's ark came to rest up on a mountain once the flood waters had gone, raised up and out of the water

explanation.surface: Deserted, like Noah's boat stranded on the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means left stranded, and literally describes a beached boat raised above the waterline.

clue.text: Storyteller's article to cause upset

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the word for cause is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to pose a problem is to cause it

explanation.surface: A teller of tales has an essay that is meant to provoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the legendary Greek author of fables, the archetypal storyteller.

clue.text: Far-flung avalanches cover the land in R. M. Ballantyne's tale

definitions.text: the land in R. M. Ballantyne's tale

indicators.note: cover says the words around the answer hide it inside them

explanation.surface: In a Victorian adventure story, avalanches cascade over a distant country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far-flung' looks like the definition of a remote place but is where the run begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungava, a region of northern Quebec, is the setting and title of Ballantyne's 1857 tale of the Eskimo country.

clue.text: Solution given by Romeo's first love?

definitions.text: Solution given by Romeo's first love?

indicators.note: given by says the solution follows the other pieces, put after them
first picks the opening letter of the name Romeo

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
saline is a salt solution, as used for drips

explanation.surface: An answer offered by the girl Romeo loved before Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run R + O + SALINE in the answer, so 'given by' puts SALINE last. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo pines for Rosaline in the opening scenes, before he ever meets Juliet.

clue.text: Moab's father's fate

definitions.meaning: in Genesis the patriarch whose elder daughter bore Moab
one's destiny or portion in life, as in to accept one's

explanation.surface: The destiny of a biblical patriarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lot fathered Moab by his elder daughter in Genesis, and one's lot is one's fate.

clue.text: Offred's one both sides in Harlem support

indicators.note: in puts the joining word between the two side letters
the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: both as in both this and that: the two sides are joined by and
aid is help or support

explanation.surface: A New York neighbourhood gives a fictional maid help on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Both sides of Harlem are H and M; 'both' gives H AND M, as in 'both this and that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Offred is the narrator of Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale, one of the women forced into service.

clue.text: Lily, a witch one might play in The Crucible?

definitions.meaning: the mother of the boy wizard in J. K. Rowling's books

definitions.text: one might play in The Crucible?
definitions.meaning: the Crucible in Sheffield hosts the world snooker championship, where players pot balls

explanation.surface: A woman named Lily who could be cast as a witch in Arthur Miller's play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible looks like Miller's witch-trial play, but it is also the Sheffield theatre that stages the world snooker championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily Potter is Harry's mother in the Harry Potter books, and a snooker player is someone who pots balls.
